conviction_note: Underwriting should land at or slightly better than the ~87% combined-ratio guide in a quarter with no US hurricane landfall. The real swing is a line most previews will skip: ASIC carries $227m (about a third of book) in a Zimmer-managed 'Absolute Return Utility & Infrastructure Fund' marked through income, and its gains made up roughly a quarter of Q2 pre-tax income. In Q3 utilities fell 13% and the 10-year rose about 100bp. That mark is uncertain and only loosely tied to the utility index (it gained in Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 when utilities were flat or down), so it leans p_up only to 45. The stock is also near its 52-week high, +12% since the last print, and sold off on its last two prints. abs_move 5.5 rests on a 4.18% median reaction with no options market and a thin float. Findings sum to -1.6; the scaled number is -0.55.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.50: Benzinga's forecast table (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ASIC/price-targets, earnings-forecasts page) and AAII's 'next-quarter consensus $0.50 from 4 analysts', with 1 downward revision in the last month and none up (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/523309-what-you-need-to-know-about-ategrity-specialty-insurance-company-holdingss-q3-earnings, 2026-10-21). Company guide from the Q2 call (Quartr summary, https://quartr.com/events/ategrity-specialty-insurance-company-holdings-asic-q2-2026_FVJLQBDs): Q3 GWP growth more than 20 points above E&S market growth, combined ratio about 87%. Two estimate sources agree, so the bar counts as sourced. ASIC's 'adjusted' EPS does NOT exclude investment gains, so the $0.50 includes whatever the Zimmer fund marks. My own arithmetic: Q3 NEP ~$120m x 13% UW margin = ~$15.6m UW income, plus ~$13m NII, less ~$1m other, taxed at ~21%, over ~49.9m diluted shares = ~$0.44-0.46 with zero investment gains. So the $0.50 needs about $4-5m of pre-tax fund gains.
positioning_check: No options market (baseline options.status no_options_market), so there is no skew and no implied move. Short interest about 275K shares, ~0.6% of float, 4.1 days to cover (Equibles, Aug 2026 settlement, https://equibles.com/stocks/asic/shortinterest). Curved Trading lists 297K shares and 3.19 days to cover at the 2026-06-30 FINRA date (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/asic/). Not a crowded short, so no squeeze mechanism. Controlled company (Zimmer Financial Services Group), so the free float is small. Average volume ~70K shares (~$1.9m/day). Tape: spot 27.38, -4.47% from the 52-week high, +4.58% over 5 days, +3.24% over 20 days, +12.0% from the 7/29 print to 10/20 against SPY +5.4% (AAII).

findings.finding: ASIC holds $227.3m at fair value through income in Zimmer Partners-managed Utility & Infrastructure Investments ($215.9m Absolute Return Utility & Infrastructure Fund plus $11.4m MidCap LP, per the Q2 10-Q). That is about 34% of $664m book value. In Q2 those investments produced $18.6m of the $46.4m pre-tax income. In Q3 2026 the S&P 500 Utilities index fell 13.0% (vs S&P 500 +2.0%) and the 10-year yield rose from 4.30% to 5.29% (Gabelli, Oct 5). The $0.50 consensus needs roughly $4-5m of positive marks; a flat or negative mark makes headline EPS about $0.35-0.46, a 10-30% miss, and dents book value per share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: History of the mark: H1 2025 -$3.2m while utilities rose about 9%; Q3 2025 +$9.2m (utilities up); Q4 2025 +$6.7m (utilities about -1.4%); Q1 2026 +$9.5m (utilities +8.3%); Q2 2026 +$18.6m (utilities +0.6%). The mark has been positive in 4 of the last 4 quarters and only loosely tied to the index. The stock has never faced a negative mark as a listed company. Reactions to the last two prints, which included large marks: -7.36% and -3.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: ASIC is +12% since the Q2 print and sits 4.5% below its 52-week high, through a quarter in which utilities fell 13%. If the market had marked the fund down, the stock would have lagged insurance peers over Q3. Coverage is 4 analysts, the line sits in a footnote-level investment table, and 1 estimate cut in the last month is the only visible hint of a lower bar.
findings.independence: The Gabelli utilities outlook (https://gabelli.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Utilities-Outlook-US-9.30.26.pdf, 2026-10-05) and Novel Investor (utilities -12.4% in Q3, https://novelinvestor.com/2026-q3-returns/, 2026-10-07) are independent of the ASIC filing but are both index proxies. The fund is 'absolute return' and may be hedged. Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 positive marks in flat or down utility quarters argue the transmission is weak, which is why this is sized at a fraction of the arithmetic.

findings.finding: The 10-year Treasury rose about 100bp in Q3 (4.30% to 5.29%). ASIC's $611.3m available-for-sale fixed-maturity book ($602.1m corporates) marks through OCI. At a 3-year duration that is roughly -$18m pre-tax, about -$0.30 of book value per share against roughly +$0.45 of retained quarterly earnings, so book value growth is flat to small in a stock that trades at about 2x book. Reinvestment yields are higher, which helps forward NII.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Book value per share has been reported each quarter: $12.24 (Q3 2025), $12.78 (Q4 2025), $13.86 (Q2 2026, +8.5% YTD). No prior quarter had a large rate-driven OCI loss.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro move every insurance analyst can model, so it is mostly priced. The remaining surprise is duration, which ASIC has not disclosed in the excerpts I read. Shares the Q2 10-Q portfolio composition with the first finding, but this is a different line (OCI, not income).
findings.independence: Portfolio size comes from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002040491/000204049126000045/asic-20260630.htm); the rate move from Gabelli/Thomson One. The duration assumption is mine and is not company-sourced.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a light catastrophe quarter for US property. No US hurricane made landfall in Q3; the season's first hurricane, Isaias, formed October 7. Travelers' Q3 cats were $538m against $695m expected. E&S peer RLI posted a Q3 combined ratio of 86.2% against a 94.7% estimate. That supports ASIC landing at or below its ~87% Q3 combined-ratio guide (Q2 was 85.9%, Q3 2025 88.7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 combined ratio 85.9% beat the 'below 87%' guide but had been pre-announced (+0.5% on the pre-announcement, -3.21% on the print). Q4 2025's 84.9% vs 92.3% came with +23.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the guide already says about 87% and peers' benign cats are public. What is left is the size of the beat against the guide. Analysts usually build in a normal cat load, so a quiet quarter shows up as a lower loss ratio. This lands inside or just better than the guided range, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Travelers' Q3 cats came in below estimates (https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/travelers-trv-q3-2026-usd-adj-eps-918-exp-739-revenue-124bln-exp-114bln). Moody's RMS on Isaias being the first US landfall since Milton (https://www.moodys.com/web/en/us/insights/insurance/moodys-rms-event-response-estimates-insured-losses-from-hurricane-isaias.html). All peer proxies; ASIC has given no Q3 cat number.

findings.finding: The E&S market is decelerating and property pricing is falling. WSIA H1 2026 surplus-lines premium rose only 2.8% (vs 13.2% a year earlier) with property -13.7%; property rates are down 25-35% in places; Kinsale's Q2 property GWP fell 32.7%. ASIC grew property GWP +21.3% in Q2 and guided Q3 GWP to more than 20 points above market (about 23%+). The risk is a softer Q4/2027 growth or margin tone on the call. A partial offset: liability, about 64% of ASIC's GWP, is hardening (non-professional liability +11.2%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ASIC restates the growth-above-market guide each quarter. The -7.36% on the Q1 2026 print and the -3.21% on Q2 came despite the guide being met, consistent with growth-durability worries in a softening market.
findings.source_date: 2026-07 (H1 2026 WSIA data, date per article title)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the market softening is well known. What is not visible yet is whether ASIC's own Q4 submission flow slowed in October. A wholesale-broker report of 'early signs of slower E&S flow in October' is paywalled and undated.
findings.independence: Kinsale's Q2 2026 release (property -32.7%; https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3434901/kinsale-capital-group-reports-second-quarter-2026-results). TheInsurer on wholesale brokers easing in Q3 (https://theinsurer.com/?p=5900, undated, paywalled). Industry proxies only.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin on the Florida Panhandle on October 9, 2026 (Category 2-3). KCC puts insured losses at about $3bn; Verisk $1-2bn; AM Best calls it an 'earnings event'. It is a Q4 loss, but management may give or be asked for a preliminary estimate on tonight's 5pm call. ASIC writes Southeast property, though its recent property growth has been in the Midwest and New England.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: no prior quarter had a named US landfall during ASIC's life as a listed company.
findings.why_not_priced: Isaias is a modest industry loss. ASIC's Florida share is undisclosed, so the market has no number to price; it surfaces only if management quantifies it.
findings.independence: Carrier Management (https://www.carriermanagement.com/news/2026/10/16/292736.htm). ASIC's own geographic mix is not sourced, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: ASIC pre-announced a beat on Q2 on July 10 (EPS >$0.60 vs $0.47 consensus, GWP >$205m), but has issued no Q3 pre-announcement before today's print. The latest 8-K is a Sept 4 item 5.02 (an employment amendment), and no 2.02 has been filed since July 29.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 10 pre-announcement (bmo): +0.5%; the Q2 print that followed: -3.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Weak signal: the Q2 pre-announcement coincided with a CFO appointment, so it is not an established practice. This is an absence, so it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: In the last month 1 of 4 analysts cut the Q3 EPS estimate and none raised it, leaving consensus at $0.50, down from the $0.55 that applied to Q2. The bar is drifting lower into the print, which partly pre-absorbs a weaker investment mark.
findings.why_not_priced: Small. A lower bar is visible to anyone with a terminal; it only partly offsets the investment-mark risk.
findings.independence: Benzinga also shows a $0.50 Q3 consensus. Same estimate data, different aggregator.

baseline_tension: No skew exists to agree or disagree with. The negative lean (investment mark, stretched run-up, two prior prints sold) cuts against the strong tape: +12% since the last print and near the 52-week high. The fund mark has defied its utility proxy before, so p_up sits only 5 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Lessons 2/5: the Zimmer fund mark is a below-the-UW-line item sized from a utility-index proxy with weak historical transmission. Shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0; kept because ASIC's adjusted EPS includes it and it reaches book value, which is the multiple's basis.
Lessons 5/6: the benign-cat finding is a peer proxy landing inside the ~87% guide. Cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Lesson 5: Isaias call disclosure is a proxy (ASIC's Florida share is unsourced). Cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 5 ('absence is not a cause'): no Q3 pre-announcement cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Lessons 6 and 7 left the rest standing: the bar is sourced from two agreeing aggregators, short interest is not crowded, and there is no skew. p_up moved from 44 to 45 and abs_move stayed at 5.5.
